text:
Nobody in the league needs a night off from the noise more than the Blackhawks. They are winless in six, outscored 32-13, and their last game was a 9-2 loss in Carolina that led to a players-only meeting Connor Bedard spoke about afterward. General manager Kyle Davidson held a press conference on Wednesday, and the week's coverage has circled the same questions: Jeff Blashill's job, and whether Chicago will use its three first-round picks to get Bedard some help. With nine points in 18 games, our playoff race gives them essentially no chance.

The fair version of the story is harsh, not hopeless. Chicago has 41% of the five-on-five expected goals, the quality of the chances, which is the league's problem area. But the goal difference (-37) is about twice as bad as the chances say it should be (-18.7), with finishing and goaltending both costing them. Spencer Knight was 11.1 goals saved above expected last season and is 2.0 below this year. Patrick Kane and Bowen Byram practiced in non-contact jerseys, per The Athletic's Scott Powers, and both have an estimated return of Nov. 14.

The bright spot has a name: Roman Kantserov. He has goals in four straight and points in eight, and his line creates 3.89 expected goals per 60 with him on the ice. He is one of our Sleepers, at 57% for a point against a season pace of 45%.

Buffalo has its own reasons to feel sore. The Sabres lost 8-3 at home to Tampa Bay last night, are on the second half of a back-to-back, and start Colten Ellis in place of Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen. They are 2-3-0 in their last five, outscored 18-13, and our race has them under 30% for the playoffs. Our other Sleeper is Jason Zucker, a third-liner with 3.1 expected goals in his last nine games, better than 99% of depth forwards; we give him a 26% chance to score against a team allowing the third-most expected goals per 60. Tage Thompson is one assist from 200. Our numbers have Buffalo at 3.27 expected goals and Chicago at 2.96.
headline: Chicago's bottom, Buffalo's tired legs
